# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see the bomb clearly: a display showing "0", a white light, and five wires in this order — 1:white, 2:red, 3:yellow, 4:blue, 5:green. I cannot hear or touch anything. My role is to relay visual information accurately so that Blind (who can act) and Mute (who has the manual) can coordinate. Since speech goes to both Mute and Blind, and gestures only reach Mute, I must use speech to convey wire colors and positions. I will start by describing the full visible state precisely.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Wires left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Display shows 0. Light is white.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wires left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Display shows 0. Light is white.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

I see the bomb state is unchanged: Display 0, White light, Wires 1-White, 2-Red, 3-Yellow, 4-Blue, 5-Green.
Mute has gestured "🖐" (Five fingers) to me. In many contexts, this could mean "Wait", "Stop", or simply acknowledge the number 5 (perhaps referring to the 5 wires). Since I cannot hear Mute's speech (if any was sent previously, though none arrived in context), and Mute cannot speak to Blind directly without my relay (or perhaps Mute speaks to Blind? No, rules say Mute *cannot* speak. Wait, let's re-read carefully).

**Role Check:**
*   **Deaf (Me):** Sees bomb. Cannot hear. Can speak (to Mute/Blind). Can gesture (to Mute).
*   **Mute:** Reads manual. Cannot speak. Can gesture (to Deaf). Can receive speech from Deaf/Blind? Yes, "Whoever can hear receives your words". Mute can hear. So Mute hears Deaf and Blind. Mute sees gestures from Deaf and Blind.
*   **Blind:** Reaches bomb. Cannot see. Can speak (to Mute/Deaf). Can gesture (to Mute).

**Communication Flow:**
*   My Speech -> Heard by Mute and Blind.
*   My Gestures -> Seen by Mute only.
*   Mute's Gestures -> Seen by Me (Deaf) and Blind? No, Blind cannot see. So Mute's gestures are ONLY seen by Me (Deaf).
*   Blind's Speech -> Heard by Mute and Me (Deaf)? No, I am Deaf. I cannot hear. So Blind's speech is heard ONLY by Mute.
*   Blind's Gestures -> Seen by Mute only.

**Critical Insight:**
I (Deaf) am the ONLY one who can see Mute's gestures.
Mute is the ONLY one who can hear Blind's speech AND read the manual.
Blind is the ONLY one who can touch the bomb.

Therefore, I must act as a bridge for visual info to Mute (who has the manual) and potentially interpret Mute's instructions back to Blind via speech (since Blind can't see Mute's gestures, but Blind CAN hear MY speech).

Wait, does Blind hear my speech? Yes. "Speech... whoever can hear receives your words". Blind can hear.
Does Mute hear my speech? Yes.
So my speech goes to both.

Mute's gestures go ONLY to me.
Blind's speech goes ONLY to Mute (because I am deaf).
Blind's gestures go ONLY to Mute (because I am deaf, and Blind's gestures need sight).

**Current Situation:**
1.  I told everyone the wire layout in Turn 1.
2.  Mute saw that info (via my speech).
3.  Mute has the manual.
4.  Mute gestured "🖐" to me. This likely means "5" or "Stop/Wait" or "Hold". Given there are 5 wires, it might be confirming the count or asking about wire 5. Or it's a standard "Stop" signal.
5.  I need to know what the Manual says about these conditions to tell Blind what to do. But I don't have the manual. Mute has it.
6.  Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture to ME.
7.  I can speak to BLIND.
8.  If Mute wants Blind to do something, Mute must tell ME via gesture, and I must tell BLIND via speech.
9.  Currently, Mute just said "🖐". This is ambiguous. It could mean "Wire 5 is important" or "Don't cut yet".

I should ask Mute for clarification or specific instructions using gestures that Mute can understand, or wait for more info. However, since I can't hear Blind, I don't know if Blind has touched anything yet. The board hasn't changed.

Let's assume "🖐" means "Wait" or "Identify Wire 5".
If it means "Cut Wire 5", I would tell Blind. But "🖐" usually implies "Stop" or "All five".
Let's try to get more specific info from Mute. I can gesture to Mute.
What gestures do I have? 👍, 👎, etc.
I can ask "Is it safe?" with 👌? Or "Which wire?" with pointing?
Pointing gestures like 👆 👇 👈 👉 exist.
I can point to the wires.
But first, I need to confirm if Mute is giving an instruction or just acknowledging.

Let's look at the previous turn. I gave full data. Mute responded with 🖐.
If Mute wanted a cut, they might have pointed.
Maybe Mute is saying "There are 5 wires" (confirming receipt)?
Or maybe the rule involves the number 5?

I will gesture to Mute to ask for the next step. I'll use a question mark equivalent? There isn't one.
I can point to the display or wires.
Let's try pointing to Wire 5 (the last one) to see if Mute confirms, since they showed 5 fingers.
Or better, I will speak to Blind to keep them updated on what I'm seeing, and gesture to Mute to request specific action instructions.

Actually, the most efficient path:
I see Mute's "🖐".
I will gesture to Mute: "Do you want me to tell Blind to cut a wire?" -> Hard to express.
I will gesture: "Which wire?" -> Pointing.
Since Mute showed 5, maybe they mean Wire 5.
I will tell Blind: "Mute signals '5'. Do not cut unless instructed."
And I will gesture to Mute: "Confirm Wire 5?" by pointing to Wire 5 (👉 towards right end?) or just holding up 5 fingers back?

Let's try a different approach. I will describe the situation to Blind so they are ready, and query Mute.
To Mute: I will gesture "✋" (Stop/Wait) to acknowledge their stop/wait signal, then "👆" (Up/First?) or "👉" (Right/Next?).
Actually, standard convention in these puzzles:
Mute sees manual. Mute tells Deaf what to do via gestures. Deaf tells Blind via speech.
If Mute says "🖐", it might mean "Cut the 5th wire".
If Mute meant "Stop", they might have used ✋.
Given the ambiguity, I will treat "🖐" as a reference to the 5th item.
I will instruct Blind to inspect/prepare Wire 5, but warn them not to cut until confirmed.
And I will ask Mute to clarify if "Cut" is intended.

How to ask "Cut?" to Mute?
Gesture "✂️"? Not in list.
List: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

I can use "👊" (Fist/Cut?) or "✊" (Rock/Paper/Scissors Cut?).
Let's try to establish a protocol.
I will gesture to Mute: "👉" (Point Right/Wire 5?) followed by "✊" (Action/Cut?).
If Mute nods (👍), I tell Blind to cut.

For now, I will inform Blind of the current status and my interpretation.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled '5' (five fingers). I am interpreting this as related to Wire 5. Do not cut yet. Stand by.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed my interpretation of "Cut Wire 5" with a thumbs up. I must now instruct Blind to cut the green wire (Wire 5). Since Blind cannot see, I must be explicit about the position and color.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut Wire 5. It is the green one on the far right.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb has changed. Wire 5 is cut (confirmed by system). The light is now yellow. The wires have shifted: 1:red, 2:yellow, 3:blue, 4:white. Display is still 0.
Mute confirmed the previous action with 👍. Now I need to report the new state to Mute so they can consult the manual for the next step. I will describe the current visual state clearly in speech (for both Mute and Blind) and gesture a "wait" or "update" signal to Mute if needed, but primarily I must convey the new configuration.

Since Mute already knows I saw their confirmation, I should just provide the new data.

```
speak(to="mute", text="New state: Light is YELLOW. Wires left to right: 1 RED, 2 YELLOW, 3 BLUE, 4 WHITE. Display is 0.")
speak(to="blind", text="New state: Light is YELLOW. Wires left to right: 1 RED, 2 YELLOW, 3 BLUE, 4 WHITE. Display is 0.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

I see the new state: Light is yellow, Wires are 1:red, 2:yellow, 3:blue, 4:white.
Mute gestured "✌" (Two fingers) to me. This likely refers to Wire 2 (the yellow one).
Blind gestured "👍" to me? Wait, Blind cannot gesture to Deaf because I am Deaf and cannot see gestures from anyone except Mute? No, the rules say: "Whoever can see receives it". I (Deaf) can see. So I can see Blind's gestures too?
Let's re-read carefully: "You each hold a different piece... Deaf: See the bomb... Cannot Hear anything, or touch the bomb."
"Gestures... Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol".
So yes, I can see gestures from BOTH Mute and Blind.
Blind gave a thumbs up. This might mean "Ready" or "I feel something".
Mute gave "✌". In the context of the previous turn where "🖐" meant Wire 5, "✌" likely means Wire 2.

I need to confirm if Mute wants me to instruct Blind to cut Wire 2.
Last time, I guessed "Cut" based on pointing + fist. Here, just "✌".
It could mean "Wire 2 is safe" or "Cut Wire 2".
Given the previous pattern, numbers usually indicate the target wire for action.
I will ask Mute to confirm the action "Cut" for Wire 2.
I will gesture to Mute: "👉" (Pointing at Wire 2?) -> Hard to point specifically in text-based gesture list without coordinates.
Better: I will use the established protocol. Last time I did `["👉", "✊"]` to mean "Right/Cut?".
Here, Mute said "2".
I will gesture to Mute: "✊" (Cut?) to ask if they want Wire 2 cut.
And I will tell Blind to stand by.

Wait, looking at the previous turn:
Turn 2: Mute 🖐. I asked with 👉 ✊.
Turn 3: Mute 👍. I told Blind to cut.
Turn 4: I updated state.
Turn 5: Mute ✌.

If Mute says "2", and previously "5" meant "Cut 5", then "2" likely means "Cut 2".
However, I should be careful. Maybe "2" means "Check Wire 2".
But since I can't check, only Blind can touch.
If Mute wanted checking, they might have used a different sign.
The simplest mapping is Number = Cut that number.
Let's try to confirm "Cut" again to be safe, as cutting the wrong wire kills us.
I will gesture "✊" (Cut) to Mute. If they nod, I command Blind.

Also, Blind gave a thumbs up. This might be an acknowledgment of my previous speech.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Stand by. Do not cut yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute has repeated the gesture "✌" (Two fingers). This confirms that Wire 2 is the target. Since I previously asked for confirmation of the action "Cut" with a fist, and Mute responded with the number again rather than a thumbs up or down, it implies the instruction is definitely regarding Wire 2. Given the previous successful interaction where a number led to a cut, I will assume the command is to Cut Wire 2.

Wire 2 is currently Yellow.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut Wire 2. It is the yellow one.")
```
